definition: An equation naming the substances in words, e.g. magnesium + oxygen -> magnesium oxide. Write one only when specifically asked; all chemical equations must be balanced.
msAccepts: equation using the names of the substances

definition: A symbol equation using formulae (e.g. 2Mg + O2 -> 2MgO); usually what is meant by 'write an equation'. Shows the proportions of reactants and products and must be balanced.
msAvoids: any list of reactants and products

definition: An equation with the same number of atoms of each element on both sides, balanced by writing big numbers in front of formulae — never by changing a formula.
msAccepts: same number of atoms of each element on both sides

definition: The big number written in front of a formula in an equation (the 2 in 2HCl); it multiplies every atom in the formula and gives the number of moles reacting.
msAccepts: big number in front of a formula
number of moles of the substance
msAvoids: number of atoms in one molecule

definition: A symbol after a formula showing physical state: (s) solid, (l) liquid, (g) gas, (aq) dissolved in water — e.g. 2K(s) + 2H2O(l) -> 2KOH(aq) + H2(g).
Dissolved in water, written (aq) after the formula. Formed when something dissolves in water; pure water itself is the liquid H2O, not aqueous.
msAvoids: the liquid state of any substance

definition: The weighted average mass of the isotopes of an element, measured on the carbon-12 scale on which a 12C atom is exactly 12. Relative masses have no units.
msAccepts: weighted average mass of isotopes on the carbon-12 scale
average mass of an atom compared with 1/12 of a 12C atom
msAvoids: a whole number for every element

definition: The comparison scale for atomic and formula masses: one atom of the carbon-12 isotope weighs exactly 12 units, so the scale's unit is one-twelfth of a 12C atom.
msAccepts: relative masses compared with a 12C atom

definition: The sum of all the relative atomic masses in a formula unit, on the carbon-12 scale; symbol Mᵣ. Used for any compound, ionic or covalent — e.g. H2O = 18, CuSO4·5H2O = 249.5.
msAccepts: sum of relative atomic masses in the formula
msAvoids: mass of one molecule in grams

definition: The Mᵣ of a substance that exists as molecules (covalent substances). Properly applied only to molecules — use relative formula mass for ionic substances like NaCl or MgO.
msAvoids: interchangeably for ionic formulae at this level

definition: The percentage by mass of an element in a compound: the element's total atom mass (atoms × Ar) divided by the compound's Mᵣ, × 100 — e.g. oxygen in Na2CO3 is 48/106 × 100.
msAccepts: percentage by mass of an element in a compound
mass of element in one mole ÷ Mᵣ × 100
msAvoids: dividing one atom's Ar by the Mᵣ ignoring subscripts

definition: Water chemically bound into a salt's crystal structure as part of its formula (the ·5H2O in CuSO4·5H2O); always fixed whole numbers per formula unit. Salts containing it are hydrated.
msAccepts: water chemically bonded in the crystal
fixed number of water molecules per formula unit
msAvoids: loose water trapped in the crystal

definition: A salt containing water of crystallisation as part of its formula, e.g. CuSO4·5H2O, Na2CO3·10H2O, MgCl2·6H2O. Its Mᵣ includes the bound water.
Without water: the salt left when all the water of crystallisation has been driven off by heating, e.g. anhydrous barium chloride, BaCl2 (no ·nH2O).
msAccepts: salt with all water of crystallisation removed

definition: The unit of amount of substance, abbreviated mol. 1 mole of a substance has a mass in grams equal to its Mᵣ and contains 6 × 10²³ particles.
msAccepts: mass of 1 mole = Mᵣ in grams
msAvoids: the same mass for every substance

definition: The number of particles in one mole of any substance: about 6 × 10²³ per mole. Equal moles of any substances contain equal numbers of particles.
msAccepts: number of particles in one mole

definition: The term commonly used for the mass of 1 mole of a substance. Strictly it has units of g/mol (the mass of 1 mole is in g), a distinction rarely needed at International GCSE.
msAccepts: the mass of 1 mole of a substance
msAvoids: a different quantity from mass of 1 mole at this level

definition: The simplest whole-number ratio of the atoms of each element present in a compound, found from mole ratios — e.g. CH2 for the compound whose molecular formula is C4H8.
msAccepts: simplest whole number ratio of atoms
msAvoids: the actual number of atoms in a molecule

definition: The actual number of atoms of each element in one molecule (or formula unit). It is the empirical formula multiplied by a whole number — e.g. H2O2 is the molecular formula with empirical HO.
msAccepts: actual number of atoms of each element
msAvoids: always different from the empirical formula

definition: Burning a substance in oxygen — the reaction type used to find the formula of magnesium oxide: the magnesium gains oxygen, so the crucible's contents increase in mass.
The removal of oxygen from a substance — used to find the formula of copper oxide by passing hydrogen over it: the oxide loses oxygen, so the dish's contents decrease in mass.
A reaction in which a more reactive element takes the place of a less reactive one in a compound — hydrogen displaces copper from copper oxide in the reduction practical.
msAccepts: a more reactive element takes the place of a less reactive one

definition: A reaction in which reduction and oxidation happen together — e.g. CuO + H2 -> Cu + H2O: the copper oxide is reduced (oxygen removed) while the hydrogen is oxidised.
actual yield ÷ theoretical yield × 100 — how much product was obtained compared with what the equation's moles promise. Should come out below 100%; above it suggests wet product or a mistake.
msAccepts: actual yield divided by theoretical yield × 100
comparison of product obtained with maximum possible

definition: The mass of product a reaction could produce, calculated from the equation and the moles of starting material — e.g. 7.53 g of CuSO4·5H2O from 2.40 g of CuO.
msAccepts: the calculated maximum mass of product
yield expected from the moles calculation

definition: The mass of product actually obtained in the experiment, given in the question — e.g. 5.21 g of crystals. Always divided by (not into) the theoretical yield for the percentage.
msAccepts: the mass obtained in the experiment

definition: Simply something that reacts. In excess calculations, try both reagents' moles in the equation: the one that runs out first (limiting) feeds the product calculation.
msAvoids: only the liquid in a reaction

definition: The reagent present in more than enough to react with all of the other one — determined from the equation's ratios, not from which amount is bigger. Removed after the reaction (e.g. by filtering).
msAccepts: more than enough to react with all the other reagent
msAvoids: whichever reagent has the larger number of moles
